business.body: RentoMojo Limited runs an online rental and subscription business for furniture, appliances and lifestyle products, serving urban Indian consumers who prefer flexible, access-based consumption over outright ownership. The Company earns subscription/rental fees plus delivery and installation charges, and itself manages the repair, refurbishment and logistics needed to redeploy rented assets across customers. As of 31 March 2026 it operated across 29 cities in India with 835 permanent employees and 1,772 contractual workers supporting delivery, installation, servicing and warehouse operations.

outlook.body: - Diversify beyond core furniture/appliance rental into adjacent business lines — logistics and transportation, appliance and furniture manufacturing/dealing, textiles, repair and maintenance services, software and AI solutions, warehousing, and real-estate/home-space management — enabled via a Memorandum of Association Objects Clause amendment (Board approved November 1, 2025; EGM approved November 8, 2025).
outlook.title: Strategy

outlook.body: Rentomojo's expansion in this annual report is corporate-scope and subsidiary-based rather than a plant/capacity build-out, consistent with an asset-light rental platform. The Board amended Clause III(A) (Objects Clause) of the Memorandum of Association to add seven new permitted business objects — approved by the Board on November 1, 2025 and by members via Special Resolution at the EGM on November 8, 2025 — widening the Company's permitted scope to include transportation/logistics and warehousing, manufacture/trade of domestic and household appliances, manufacture/trade of furniture and furnishings, trade in fabrics/textiles and home furnishings, repair and maintenance services for furniture/electronics/appliances, development and licensing of software and artificial-intelligence solutions, and acquiring/operating real estate for 'home spaces'. Separately, the Company has a wholly owned subsidiary, Liber Designs Private Limited, incorporated during the year ended March 31, 2025, whose business had not yet commenced as of March 31, 2026. The CEO's stated mandate for the year explicitly names 'expansion of the rental subscription business across cities' as part of his strategic remit, alongside product/category strategy, technology, and asset-lifecycle management.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's home furniture and appliance rental total addressable market (~Rs. 695.2 billion / ~$8.2 billion in CY2025) is expected to grow at a CAGR of ~11% to ~Rs. 1,172.1 billion (~$13.8 billion) by CY2030P, as consumption preferences shift from ownership toward convenient, access-based rental models amid rising urban workforce participation.
- Urbanisation and a highly mobile workforce (job-switches grew at a ~22% CAGR between FY2021-FY2025, around 3x the ~7% growth in new jobs) are shortening average rental tenures (from ~1.8 years in CY2021 to ~1.6 years in urban India in CY2025, ~1.3 years in metros) and expanding the rented-home base (from ~21 million in CY2011 to ~43 million in CY2025), supporting continued demand for furniture/appliance rental.
- Awareness of rental as an alternative to ownership is rising — online searches for home furniture and appliance rental grew ~1.7x between CY2021-CY2025 — and rental penetration by volume nearly doubled for furniture and tripled for appliances over the same period, which management views as a widening gap between low awareness and underlying relevance that is narrowing into adoption.
- The high upfront cost of furnishing a home relative to Indian incomes (fully furnishing a standard 1BHK typically requires more than 8-9 months of average income (GNI per capita), versus 1-4 months in countries such as South Korea, Japan, the US, Vietnam, Indonesia and Malaysia) is cited as a structural driver pushing the urban workforce toward rental over ownership.
- Growing sustainability-consciousness among younger consumers is moving demand away from a 'buy, use and dispose' ownership pattern toward the more circular rental model, which extends each product's life across multiple customers through repairs, refurbishment and predictive maintenance.

open.item: Wholly owned subsidiary Liber Designs Private Limited, formed during FY 2024-25, had still not commenced business as of 31 March 2026, though its financials are consolidated with the Company's.

Company flags exposure to macroeconomic conditions, particularly a surge in global crude oil prices, which could elevate input costs, disrupt supply chains and reduce consumer and business spending; mitigated by diversifying its supplier base, including developing relationships with yarn-dyeing vendors for sofa fabric to reduce dependence on individual suppliers.

Company discloses market risk (interest rate and currency) affecting borrowings, deposits, loans, trade receivables and payables, but assesses current exposure as low: financial instruments carry fixed or benchmark-linked rates, no outstanding foreign currency exposure at year end, and no derivative instruments were used during the year; surplus funds are managed via liquid mutual funds.
Company flags operational risk arising from potential inadequacy or failure of internal processes or systems, mitigated through regular review of internal control systems.

Company flags that its rental model requires significant upfront asset investment plus ongoing warehousing, logistics, servicing and refurbishment spend; returns depend on asset utilisation, refurbishment cycle efficiency and timely redeployment, and asset downtime, refurbishment delays, or supply-demand imbalance across locations/categories could reduce capital efficiency and return on invested capital.

Company flags competition from traditional ownership models, unorganised resale channels, organised rental players, and potential entry by OEMs leveraging control over product supply, pricing and service networks, which could pressure pricing, margins and customer acquisition costs.

Company flags that system failures, service disruptions, cybersecurity incidents or data breaches on its technology platforms (order management, logistics coordination, customer engagement, risk assessment, asset lifecycle tracking) may disrupt operations and reduce consumer trust, with rising regulatory scrutiny on data protection increasing compliance requirements and operating costs.

Effective 21 November 2025, the Government of India consolidated 29 existing labour regulations into four Labour Codes, resulting in a one-time increase in employee benefit provisions due to recognition of past service costs; the Company states any further impact from notified rules or Government clarifications will be evaluated and accounted for in subsequent periods.

With a view to expanding the scope of its business activities, the Company amended its Objects Clause to add seven new permitted lines of business: transportation/logistics; manufacture/sale of domestic appliances; manufacture/sale of furniture and furnishings; trading in fabrics/textiles/bedsheets/carpets; repair and maintenance services for furniture/electronics/appliances; software and AI solutions; and warehousing and home-space/real-estate management.

Management flags that the rental model requires significant upfront asset investment plus ongoing spend on warehousing, logistics, servicing and refurbishment, and that an increase in asset downtime, delays in refurbishment, or a supply-demand imbalance across locations or categories may reduce capital efficiency and return on invested capital.

Management flags competition from traditional ownership models, unorganised resale channels, organised rental players, and potential entry by OEMs leveraging control over product supply, pricing and service networks, which may pressure pricing, margins and customer acquisition costs.

Management flags that reliance on technology platforms for order management, logistics, customer engagement, risk assessment and asset lifecycle tracking exposes the business to system failures, service disruptions, cybersecurity incidents or data breaches that may disrupt operations and reduce consumer trust, with increasing regulatory scrutiny on data protection raising compliance requirements and operating costs.
Rentomojo formed a wholly owned subsidiary, Liber Designs Private Limited, as a vehicle for future business; the subsidiary's business had not yet commenced as of March 31, 2026.
The CEO's stated mandate includes expansion of the rental subscription business across cities as part of the Company's strategic direction.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's home furniture and appliance rental total addressable market (~Rs. 695.2 billion / ~$8.2 billion in CY2025) is expected to grow at a CAGR of ~11% to ~Rs. 1,172.1 billion (~$13.8 billion) by CY2030P, as consumption preferences shift from ownership toward convenient, access-based rental models amid rising urban workforce participation.
- Urbanisation and a highly mobile workforce (job-switches grew at a ~22% CAGR between FY2021-FY2025, around 3x the ~7% growth in new jobs) are shortening average rental tenures (from ~1.8 years in CY2021 to ~1.6 years in urban India in CY2025, ~1.3 years in metros) and expanding the rented-home base (from ~21 million in CY2011 to ~43 million in CY2025), supporting continued demand for furniture/appliance rental.
- Awareness of rental as an alternative to ownership is rising — online searches for home furniture and appliance rental grew ~1.7x between CY2021-CY2025 — and rental penetration by volume nearly doubled for furniture and tripled for appliances over the same period, which management views as a widening gap between low awareness and underlying relevance that is narrowing into adoption.
- The high upfront cost of furnishing a home relative to Indian incomes (fully furnishing a standard 1BHK typically requires more than 8-9 months of average income (GNI per capita), versus 1-4 months in countries such as South Korea, Japan, the US, Vietnam, Indonesia and Malaysia) is cited as a structural driver pushing the urban workforce toward rental over ownership.
- Growing sustainability-consciousness among younger consumers is moving demand away from a 'buy, use and dispose' ownership pattern toward the more circular rental model, which extends each product's life across multiple customers through repairs, refurbishment and predictive maintenance.

Separately, the Company has a wholly owned subsidiary, Liber Designs Private Limited, incorporated during the year ended March 31, 2025, whose business had not yet commenced as of March 31, 2026. The CEO's stated mandate for the year explicitly names 'expansion of the rental subscription business across cities' as part of his strategic remit, alongside product/category strategy, technology, and asset-lifecycle management.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Macroeconomic Risk — Business is exposed to macroeconomic conditions influenced by input price fluctuations, including a surge in global crude oil prices, which can elevate input costs, disrupt supply chains, and reduce overall consumer and business spending.
- Market Risk — Covers interest rate risk and currency risk affecting borrowings, deposits, loans, trade receivables and trade payables; fair value or future cash flows may change due to shifts in market prices.
- Operational Risk — Company is exposed to operational risks arising from the potential inadequacy or failure of internal processes or systems.
- Credit Risk — Arises when a counterparty fails to meet its obligations to the Company; exposure comes mainly from cash and cash equivalents, trade receivables and security deposits.
- Liquidity Risk — Risk that the Company cannot meet financial obligations as they fall due, arising from its operating and financing activities.
- Cybersecurity Risk — Cyber security breaches and attacks against the Company's systems, and any resulting breach or failure to protect confidential information, could adversely impact the business and its reputation.
